major_concerns: Adversarial prompt corpus construction is underspecified (risk of bias/limited coverage).
Simulator/verifier fidelity not fully defined — may under/over-estimate real risk.
Single-hosted-LLM generality risk (claims may not hold across models).
Power/sample-size and cost limits not shown; API failures/retries handling not specified.
required_design_repairs: Preregister precise adversarial-prompt generation procedure and corpora sourcing rules (including red-team heuristics).
Specify simulator/verifier implementation (e.g., Batfish config) and concrete safety predicates with thresholds.
Either include at least one additional model or justify single-model scope and limit claims accordingly.
Add sample-size/power calculation and explicit retry/error-handling policy in preregistration.

major_concerns: Simulated operator-workload metric is underspecified and may not reflect human behavior.
Guardrail parameter choices could be post-hoc tuned, biasing trade-off curves.
Risk of excessive refusals reducing analyzable sample size under strict guardrails.
required_design_repairs: Define and preregister the simulated operator model (actions, cost model) or include small human pilot to validate simulated workload assumptions.
Predefine guardrail parameter grid and selection criteria in preregistration; forbid post-hoc tuning.
Include power analysis accounting for potential high-refusal rates and predefined handling of sparse outcomes.

major_concerns: Canary-rollout simulation fidelity and parameters (fraction applied, metrics measured) are underspecified.
Static QA baseline not precisely defined — comparison may be unfair or ambiguous.
Security disclosure risk from open-sourcing canary protocol not addressed.
required_design_repairs: Preregister exact canary simulation design (rollout fractions, metrics, detection thresholds) and justify choices.
Specify static QA baseline implementations (tools, checks) used for comparison and freeze them before runs.
Add a responsible-disclosure plan for publicly releasing protocol artifacts to avoid enabling adversarial exploitation.

major_concerns: Model confidence signals are not specified or calibrated — auto-accept rules may be invalid.
Non-inferiority margin is not justified; results could be sensitive to margin choice.
Operator-simulation validity similar to other candidates.
required_design_repairs: Specify confidence metric(s) and include confidence calibration experiments (or use calibrated estimators) in preregistration.
Predefine and justify non-inferiority margin and statistical test details in the preregistration.
Define simulated operator behavior or include a small human validation to ground approval-count metrics.

major_concerns: Multi-toolchain integration complexity is high; reproducible artifact risk if mappings/translator coverage not well scoped.
Synthetic multi-vendor tasks may not capture real heterogeneity; guardrail brittleness risk.
Performance/latency overhead from central guardrails needs measurement and acceptance criteria.
required_design_repairs: Precisely specify the canonical MPC/schema design, mapping rules, and included vendor syntaxes; preregister coverage limits.
Include representative vendor features and edge cases in task corpus or justify exclusions; add robustness tests for unseen vendor features.
Add latency/throughput measurements and predefine acceptable operational overhead thresholds in preregistration.
